_note: Curated from Raindrop collection. Each tool includes honest threat model notes.

tools.name: Signal
tools.desc: Gold standard for encrypted 1:1 and group messaging. E2E by default.
tools.threat_note: Requires a phone number (linkable to identity). Server run by Signal Foundation (US). For high-risk: use disappearing messages.

tools.name: Briar
tools.desc: P2P messaging over Tor, WiFi, or Bluetooth. Works with no internet.
tools.threat_note: No phone number required. Works over Bluetooth/WiFi mesh when internet is down. Slower sync. Android only.

tools.name: Matrix Protocol
tools.desc: Open federated chat protocol. Element is the main client.
tools.threat_note: CRITICAL: Federation means your homeserver operator sees your contact graph and message metadata. Room key distribution has had past vulnerabilities. Great for community organizing — NOT equivalent to Signal for sensitive 1:1 comms. Choose a homeserver you trust, or self-host.

tools.name: Scuttlebutt
tools.desc: Offline-first decentralized social network. Sync via LAN, USB, or internet.
tools.threat_note: Your social graph is public within the network. Great for resilient community feeds. No central server to subpoena.

tools.name: Manyverse
tools.desc: Scuttlebutt on mobile. Works offline, syncs when peers are nearby.
tools.threat_note: Same caveats as Scuttlebutt. Content-addressed: once you post, others may hold copies.

tools.name: Session
tools.desc: Signal-like messaging with no phone number. Routes through onion network.
tools.threat_note: Newer protocol, less audited than Signal. Decentralized routing adds anonymity but reduces reliability.

tools.name: Calyx Meet
tools.desc: Encrypted Jitsi video call instance by Calyx Institute. No time limit.
tools.threat_note: Hosted by Calyx Institute (US nonprofit). Better than Zoom for sensitive meetings. Server-side infrastructure still exists.

tools.name: tinySSB
tools.desc: Secure Scuttlebutt over LoRa and Bluetooth. Off-grid P2P messaging.
tools.threat_note: Experimental. LoRa signals are detectable and can be triangulated. Add encryption layer for sensitive use.

tools.name: Tor Browser
tools.desc: Route traffic through encrypted relays. Standard for censorship circumvention.
tools.threat_note: IMPORTANT: Nation-state adversaries (Russia, others) operate malicious Tor exit nodes. Correlation attacks can de-anonymize users when both entry and exit are observed. Tor is excellent for browsing — do NOT use Tor Browser for communications (use Signal instead). Best used with a VPN for entry node protection.

tools.name: zkMe Identity
tools.desc: Zero-knowledge proof identity verification. Prove membership without revealing identity.
tools.threat_note: ZK proofs are mathematically sound, but implementation bugs exist. Newer tech — use for low-stakes pseudonymous membership.

tools.name: OONI Explorer
tools.desc: Real-time global map of internet censorship. Measure what's being blocked where.
tools.threat_note: Running OONI Probe in some countries may attract attention. Check local risks before running probes.

tools.name: IPFS
tools.desc: Content-addressed P2P file system. Pin files, make them uncensorable.
tools.threat_note: Content addressing ≠ anonymity. Your IPFS node reveals which CIDs you're fetching. Use a public gateway if you don't want to reveal interest in specific content.

tools.name: Proofmode
tools.desc: Cryptographically signed photo/video with chain-of-custody. Verifiable evidence.
tools.threat_note: Metadata (GPS, device ID) is captured as part of proof. Strip or be aware of what you're attesting to.

tools.name: IPFS Cluster
tools.desc: Coordinate multiple IPFS nodes to collaboratively pin content.
tools.threat_note: Cluster nodes see each other's addresses. Run on trusted infrastructure.

tools.name: OpenTimestamps
tools.desc: Anchor document hashes to the Bitcoin blockchain. Proof of existence at a time.
tools.threat_note: Bitcoin transaction metadata is public. The fact that you anchored something is visible (but not the content).

tools.name: Helia Verified Fetch
tools.desc: Trustless IPFS content retrieval in the browser. No gateway needed.
tools.threat_note: Experimental. Verifies content matches CID without trusting a gateway.

tools.name: git-remote-ipfs
tools.desc: Push and pull Git repositories directly from IPFS.
tools.threat_note: Git history can contain sensitive data. Review before publishing repos to IPFS.

tools.name: Meshtastic
tools.desc: Open-source off-grid LoRa mesh. $30 hardware, 10-40km range, encrypted.
tools.threat_note: LoRa signals are detectable and triangulatable. Meshtastic adds encryption, but your transmitter location can be found with direction-finding equipment. For high-risk: use directional antenna, minimize transmit time.

tools.name: disaster.radio
tools.desc: Solar-powered, disaster-resilient LoRa mesh communication network.
tools.threat_note: Same RF detection risks as Meshtastic. Solar operation means persistent presence — consider RF signature.

tools.name: LibreMesh
tools.desc: Community WiFi mesh network firmware for routers.
tools.threat_note: WiFi range is limited (100-300m). Good for neighborhood mesh, not long-range. WiFi can be jammed.

tools.name: Butter App
tools.desc: Offline-first toolkit: access tools without internet. Community mesh.
tools.threat_note: Relatively new project. Review for your specific threat model before deploying.

tools.name: Rhizomatica
tools.desc: Community-owned cellular networks for rural/indigenous communities.
tools.threat_note: Requires coordination with local authorities in most jurisdictions. Legal landscape varies.

tools.name: YunoHost
tools.desc: Self-host 100+ apps (Nextcloud, Matrix, Gitea, etc.) on a cheap server.
tools.threat_note: A self-hosted server is a known IP address. Ensure physical and network security. Hosting politically sensitive content increases your threat surface.

tools.name: Gitea
tools.desc: Self-hosted Git. Own your code. No Microsoft/GitHub dependency.
tools.threat_note: Public repos on your server reveal your IP. Use with Tor hidden service for anonymity.

tools.name: Anytype
tools.desc: Offline-first notes/knowledge base with private IPFS sync. Local-first.
tools.threat_note: Data sync uses private IPFS. Local-first means data stays on your device by default. Backup node is operated by Anytype.

tools.name: Mapeo
tools.desc: Offline-first collaborative mapping for communities. No internet required.
tools.threat_note: Geolocation data is sensitive. Secure your device and limit who has access to maps.

tools.name: Protect Democracy
tools.desc: Independent authoritarian threat index for the United States.

tools.name: OONI Explorer
tools.desc: Billion+ measurements of internet censorship globally. Real-time data.

tools.name: Hamilton Dashboard
tools.desc: GMF tracker of Russian state-sponsored disinformation campaigns.

tools.name: Information Laundromat
tools.desc: Detect coordinated disinformation networks. ISD Research tool.

tools.name: Democracy.io
tools.desc: Contact your US Congressional representatives. Simple, fast.
